meta.title: Two's company: why Switzerland will not let a guinea pig live alone
meta.deck: Swiss law treats loneliness as a form of cruelty, at least for certain small, furry creatures.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Two's company: why Switzerland will not let a guinea pig live alone
sents.zh: 两个才叫伴：为什么瑞士不让豚鼠独自生活
notes: Two's company：来自俗语 two's company, three's a crowd（两人成伴，三人不欢），这里反过来强调“两个才够”。
guinea pig：豚鼠（荷兰猪）；也比喻“试验品”。

sents.en: Swiss law treats loneliness as a form of cruelty, at least for certain small, furry creatures.
sents.zh: 瑞士法律把孤独视为一种虐待，至少对某些毛茸茸的小动物是这样。
notes: treat A as B：把 A 当作 B。
cruelty：残忍、虐待。
at least for ...：至少对……来说，补充限定范围。

sents.en: Owners have had to adjust, and at least one entrepreneur has spotted a gap in the market.
sents.zh: 主人们不得不适应，而至少有一位创业者从中发现了商机。
notes: have had to：不得不（现在完成时）。
entrepreneur：创业者、企业家。
a gap in the market：市场空白、商机。

sents.en: Switzerland has a reputation for meticulous rules, and its animal-welfare laws are among the strictest anywhere.
sents.zh: 瑞士以规定细致入微出名，它的动物福利法也是全世界最严格的之一。
notes: have a reputation for：以……出名。
meticulous：一丝不苟的、极其细致的。
among the strictest anywhere：在任何地方都算最严格的之一。

sents.en: Since 2008 they have obliged owners of sociable species, guinea pigs included, to keep them with at least one of their own kind.
sents.zh: 自 2008 年起，这些法律要求群居动物（包括豚鼠）的主人，至少要让它们和一只同类住在一起。
notes: oblige sb to do：要求、迫使某人做……（已学）。
sociable：爱交际的；（动物）群居的。
guinea pigs included：插入成分，“豚鼠也包括在内”。one's own kind：同类。

sents.en: A solitary guinea pig, the thinking goes, is a forlorn one.
sents.zh: 人们的想法是：一只孤零零的豚鼠，就是一只可怜兮兮的豚鼠。
notes: solitary：独自的、孤零零的。
the thinking goes：插入语，“按照这种想法”（类似学过的 the logic goes）。
forlorn：孤苦伶仃的、可怜的。one 代替 guinea pig。

sents.en: The animals squeak, groom each other and huddle together for warmth; deprived of company, they can become listless and withdrawn.
sents.zh: 这些小动物会吱吱叫、互相梳理毛发、挤在一起取暖；一旦没了同伴，它们可能变得无精打采、孤僻退缩。
notes: squeak：吱吱叫。groom：（动物）梳理毛发。
huddle together：挤成一团。
deprived of company：过去分词短语表示条件，“如果失去陪伴”。listless：无精打采的。withdrawn：孤僻的、不合群的。

sents.en: The rule creates an awkward dilemma when one of a pair dies.
sents.zh: 当一对豚鼠中有一只死去时，这条规定就带来了一个尴尬的两难局面。
notes: dilemma：两难的处境。
one of a pair：一对中的一只。

sents.en: Buying a replacement solves the immediate problem but starts the cycle again, since the newcomer will probably outlive its elderly companion.
sents.zh: 再买一只能解决眼前的问题，但又会让循环重新开始，因为新来的那只很可能比年老的同伴活得更久。
notes: Buying a replacement：动名词短语作主语。
the immediate problem：眼前的问题。
outlive：比……活得长。companion：同伴。

sents.en: Owners can end up trapped in an endless chain of guinea pigs, each new purchase prolonging the obligation by several years.
sents.zh: 主人们可能陷入一条没完没了的“豚鼠链”，每买一只新的，就让这份责任又延长好几年。
notes: end up trapped in：最后被困在……（end up 已学）。
each new purchase prolonging ...：独立主格结构，补充说明结果。
prolong：延长。obligation：义务、责任。

sents.en: Some resort to scouring online adverts for an elderly animal that needs a home.
sents.zh: 有人不得不在网上广告里四处搜寻，想找一只需要人收养的老年豚鼠。
notes: resort to doing：不得已采取……。
scour ... for ...：彻底搜寻……以找到……。
advert：（英式）广告，= advertisement。

sents.en: Into this niche stepped a breeder who began renting out guinea pigs.
sents.zh: 就在这个缝隙里，一位饲养者站了出来，开始出租豚鼠。
notes: Into this niche stepped a breeder：地点状语提前，主谓倒装（见语法点）。
niche：（市场的）空白、小众领域。
breeder：饲养者、育种人。rent out：出租。

sents.en: A bereaved animal can be paired with a hired companion of a suitable age; when it eventually dies, the lodger goes back and is put up for hire again.
sents.zh: 失去伴侣的豚鼠可以配上一只年龄合适的“租来的伙伴”；等它最终离世，这位“房客”就被送回去，再次出租。
notes: bereaved：丧失亲人的。
be paired with：和……配成一对。hired：租来的。
lodger：房客、寄宿者。put up for hire：拿出来出租。

sents.en: The arrangement sounds faintly comic, yet it addresses a genuine welfare problem.
sents.zh: 这种安排听上去有点滑稽，但它确实解决了一个真实存在的动物福利问题。
notes: faintly：有点儿、略微。
address a problem：处理、解决问题。
genuine：真正的。

sents.en: Guinea pigs are not the only beneficiaries of Swiss solicitude.
sents.zh: 享受到瑞士这份关怀的，不只有豚鼠。
notes: beneficiary：受益者。
solicitude：（正式）关切、关怀。

sents.en: Budgerigars and other flock birds are likewise entitled to company of their own species.
sents.zh: 虎皮鹦鹉和其他群居鸟类，同样有权拥有同类的陪伴。
notes: budgerigar：虎皮鹦鹉，口语叫 budgie。
flock：（鸟、羊）群。likewise：同样地。
be entitled to：有权享有（entitle 已学）。

sents.en: In 2018 the government banned the practice of plunging live lobsters into boiling water; they must now be stunned first.
sents.zh: 2018 年，政府禁止把活龙虾直接扔进沸水；现在必须先把它们弄晕。
notes: ban the practice of doing：禁止……的做法。
plunge ... into ...：把……猛地投入……。
stun：使昏迷、打晕。

sents.en: For several years, new dog owners even had to sit a short course before bringing a puppy home, though that requirement has since been scrapped.
sents.zh: 有好几年，新养狗的人甚至要先上一门短期课程，才能把小狗带回家，不过这项要求后来取消了。
notes: sit a course / an exam：参加课程、考试（英式）。
though ...：不过……，补充转折。
has since been scrapped：后来被取消了（scrap 已学）。

sents.en: Critics deride all this as the nanny state run amok.
sents.zh: 批评者嘲笑这一切是“保姆式国家”管过了头。
notes: deride A as B：嘲笑 A 是 B。
the nanny state：保姆式国家，指政府管得太多（已学）。
run amok：失控、乱来；这里 run 是过去分词，修饰 nanny state。

sents.en: Why, they ask, should bureaucrats dictate how many rodents a family keeps?
sents.zh: 他们质问：凭什么要官僚来规定一家人养几只啮齿动物？
notes: they ask 是插入语。
bureaucrat：官僚、政府官员。
dictate：规定、命令。rodent：啮齿动物（老鼠、豚鼠等）。

sents.en: Defenders counter that a pet is not a toy, and that an animal cannot lodge a complaint about its own living conditions.
sents.zh: 支持者反驳说，宠物不是玩具，而且动物也没办法为自己的生活条件提出投诉。
notes: counter that ...：反驳说……。
两个 that 从句并列，都是 counter 的宾语。
lodge a complaint：正式提出投诉。

sents.en: Most Swiss seem untroubled either way.
sents.zh: 不管怎样，大多数瑞士人似乎都不太在意。
notes: untroubled：不受困扰的、无所谓的。
either way：不管怎样（已学）。

sents.en: In a country that prizes privacy and quiet, it seems fitting that even its smallest residents are guaranteed a friend.
sents.zh: 在一个珍视隐私和安静的国家，就连最小的居民也被保证有一个朋友，这似乎也挺合适。
notes: prize 作动词：珍视。
it seems fitting that ...：……似乎很恰当，it 是形式主语。
resident：居民，这里俏皮地指豚鼠。

vocab.note: 完整俗语是 two's company, three's a crowd：两个人在一起正好，第三个人就多余了（常指情侣不想有电灯泡）。

ex.en: I'll leave you two alone; [[two's company]], three's a crowd.
ex.zh: 我就不打扰你们俩了，两人成伴，三人不欢嘛。

ex.en: They never invite anyone else; [[two's company]] for them.
ex.zh: 他们从不叫别人，两个人就够了。

vocab.def: a saying meaning that two people are happy together and a third person is not wanted

vocab.note: 一种小型宠物鼠，中文也叫荷兰猪。也常比喻“试验品、被拿来做实验的人”：be a guinea pig / use sb as guinea pigs。注意 guinea 读 /ˈɡɪnɪ/，像“gi-ni”。

ex.en: My daughter wants a [[guinea pig]] for her birthday.
ex.zh: 我女儿生日想要一只豚鼠。

ex.en: I don't want to be a [[guinea pig]] for a new drug.
ex.zh: 我可不想当新药的试验品。

ex.en: The students were used as [[guinea pigs]] for the new teaching method.
ex.zh: 这些学生被拿来当新教学法的试验品。

vocab.def: a small furry animal with no tail, often kept as a pet; also, a person used in a test or experiment

cf.diff: guinea pig 是豚鼠，体型较大、没有尾巴、爱群居；hamster 是仓鼠，体型小、常独居。

ex.en: Our [[hamster]] runs on its wheel all night.
ex.zh: 我们家的仓鼠整晚都在跑轮上跑。

vocab.note: 形容词 cruel（残忍的）。cruelty to animals（虐待动物）。

ex.en: The farm was closed after reports of [[cruelty]] to animals.
ex.zh: 有人举报虐待动物后，这个农场被关闭了。

ex.en: I was shocked by the [[cruelty]] of the punishment.
ex.zh: 这种惩罚之残忍让我震惊。

vocab.def: behaviour that causes pain or suffering to people or animals on purpose

vocab.note: 自己开公司、敢冒险做生意的人。形容词 entrepreneurial（有创业精神的）。注意拼写 -eur 结尾。

ex.en: She became a successful [[entrepreneur]] at 25.
ex.zh: 她 25 岁就成了成功的创业者。

ex.en: The city wants to attract young [[entrepreneurs]].
ex.zh: 这座城市想吸引年轻的创业者。

vocab.def: a person who starts a business, especially one that involves risk

vocab.expr: spot a gap in the market
vocab.zh: 发现商机、发现市场空白
m: spotted a gap in the market
vocab.note: spot = 发现、看出（尤其是别人没注意到的东西）。a gap in the market：市场上还没人提供的东西，也就是商机。也可以说 see / find a gap in the market。
vocab.core: spot a gap in the market
forms: spot a gap in the market
spots a gap in the market
spotted a gap in the market
spotting a gap in the market

ex.en: He [[spotted a gap in the market]] for cheap healthy lunches.
ex.zh: 他发现便宜健康的午餐是个市场空白。

ex.en: Good entrepreneurs are quick at [[spotting a gap in the market]].
ex.zh: 好的创业者很快就能发现商机。

vocab.def: to notice a chance to sell a product or service that nobody else is offering

vocab.zh: 一丝不苟的、极其细致的
vocab.note: 非常注意细节、很仔细：meticulous planning（周密的计划）。副词 meticulously。

ex.en: She keeps [[meticulous]] records of her spending.
ex.zh: 她把每笔开销都记得清清楚楚。

ex.en: The plan was prepared with [[meticulous]] care.
ex.zh: 这份计划准备得一丝不苟。

vocab.def: very careful about every small detail

cf.diff: meticulous 是连小细节都极其仔细；careless 是粗心大意、不小心。

ex.en: It was a [[careless]] mistake.
ex.zh: 这是个粗心造成的错误。

vocab.note: welfare 是“福利、健康幸福”。animal welfare 指让动物不受虐待、生活得好。作定语时常加连字符：animal-welfare laws。

ex.en: She works for an [[animal welfare]] charity.
ex.zh: 她在一家动物福利慈善机构工作。

ex.en: The zoo was criticised over [[animal welfare]].
ex.zh: 这家动物园因为动物福利问题受到批评。

vocab.def: the health and happiness of animals, and the rules that protect them

vocab.note: of one's own kind：和自己同一类的（人或动物）。

ex.en: Cats usually prefer [[their own kind]].
ex.zh: 猫通常更喜欢和同类在一起。

ex.en: He only feels comfortable among [[his own kind]].
ex.zh: 他只有在同类人中间才自在。

vocab.def: people or animals of the same type as yourself

vocab.note: 强调“单独一个”，不一定难过：a solitary walk（独自散步）、solitary animals（独居动物）。

ex.en: Tigers are [[solitary]] animals.
ex.zh: 老虎是独居动物。

ex.en: He enjoys long, [[solitary]] walks.
ex.zh: 他喜欢独自长时间散步。

vocab.def: alone, without other people or animals; done alone

cf.diff: solitary 只是客观地说“独自一个”；lonely 强调心里觉得孤单、难过。

ex.en: She felt [[lonely]] in the new city.
ex.zh: 她在新城市觉得很孤单。

vocab.note: 看起来又孤单又难过：a forlorn figure（孤零零的身影）。也指希望渺茫：a forlorn hope。

ex.en: A [[forlorn]] dog waited outside the shop.
ex.zh: 一只可怜的狗在店外等着。

ex.en: He looked [[forlorn]] after his friends left.
ex.zh: 朋友们走后，他看上去孤零零的。

vocab.def: lonely and unhappy; looking sad and left alone

vocab.note: 老鼠、豚鼠的叫声，或门、鞋发出的尖细声音：The door squeaks.（门吱吱响。）

ex.en: The mouse [[squeaked]] and ran away.
ex.zh: 老鼠吱地一声跑了。

ex.en: My new shoes [[squeak]] when I walk.
ex.zh: 我的新鞋走路时吱吱响。

vocab.def: to make a short, high sound

vocab.note: 动物用舌头、爪子给自己或同伴理毛；人给宠物梳毛也用 groom。名词还有“新郎”（= bridegroom）。

ex.en: Monkeys spend hours [[grooming]] each other.
ex.zh: 猴子会花好几个小时互相理毛。

ex.en: She [[grooms]] her dog every Sunday.
ex.zh: 她每周日给狗梳毛。

vocab.def: (of an animal) to clean the fur of itself or another animal

vocab.note: huddle together / huddle around：因为冷或害怕挤在一起。

ex.en: We [[huddled]] around the fire to keep warm.
ex.zh: 我们围着火挤在一起取暖。

ex.en: The penguins [[huddle]] together in winter.
ex.zh: 企鹅冬天挤在一起。

vocab.def: to move close together in a group, often because of cold or fear

cf.diff: cuddle 是两个人亲密地搂抱（表达爱）；huddle 是一群人或动物挤在一起，多因为冷或害怕。

ex.en: She [[cuddled]] her baby.
ex.zh: 她搂着宝宝。

vocab.note: 没精神、对什么都提不起兴趣，常因为生病、天热或难过。

ex.en: The heat made everyone feel [[listless]].
ex.zh: 炎热让大家都没精打采的。

ex.en: The sick puppy lay [[listless]] in its basket.
ex.zh: 生病的小狗无精打采地躺在篮子里。

vocab.def: having no energy or interest in anything

cf.diff: listless 是没精神、懒得动；restless 正相反，是静不下来、坐立不安。

ex.en: The children grew [[restless]] on the long journey.
ex.zh: 长途旅行中孩子们开始坐不住了。

vocab.note: 形容人或动物变得安静、不和人交往。注意 withdraw 是“取（钱）、撤回”（已学），withdrawn 作形容词是“孤僻的”。

ex.en: After the accident he became very [[withdrawn]].
ex.zh: 出事后，他变得很孤僻。

ex.en: She's a shy, [[withdrawn]] child.
ex.zh: 她是个害羞、不爱说话的孩子。

vocab.def: quiet and not wanting to talk to or be with others

vocab.note: out- 表示“超过”：outlive sb（比某人活得久）。类似 outrun（跑得比……快，已学）。

ex.en: She [[outlived]] her husband by twenty years.
ex.zh: 她比丈夫多活了二十年。

ex.en: Parrots can [[outlive]] their owners.
ex.zh: 鹦鹉可能比主人活得还久。

vocab.def: to live longer than someone or something

vocab.note: 让时间、过程变得更长：prolong your life（延长寿命）。形容词 prolonged（长时间的）。

ex.en: Exercise can help [[prolong]] your life.
ex.zh: 锻炼有助于延长寿命。

ex.en: They [[prolonged]] their holiday by a week.
ex.zh: 他们把假期延长了一周。

vocab.def: to make something last longer

cf.diff: extend 很常用，可以延长时间，也可以扩大范围（extend the road）；prolong 只用于时间，常带“拖长”的意味。

ex.en: Can I [[extend]] my visa?
ex.zh: 我可以延长签证吗？

vocab.note: 因为法律、承诺或道德必须做的事：feel an obligation to help（觉得有义务帮忙）。动词 oblige（已学）。

ex.en: You are under no [[obligation]] to buy anything.
ex.zh: 您没有义务买任何东西。

ex.en: Parents have an [[obligation]] to look after their children.
ex.zh: 父母有义务照顾孩子。

vocab.def: something that you must do because of a law, a promise or a duty

vocab.note: resort to + 名词 / doing：没别的办法时才用某种手段：resort to violence（诉诸暴力）。

ex.en: In the end, they [[resorted to]] selling the car.
ex.zh: 最后他们不得已卖了车。

ex.en: I hope we won't have to [[resort to]] legal action.
ex.zh: 希望我们不必诉诸法律。

vocab.def: to do something you would rather not do, because there is no other way

vocab.note: scour sth for sth：为了找某物把某地仔细搜个遍：scour the internet for deals（满网找便宜）。本义是用力擦洗。

ex.en: Police [[scoured]] the woods for the missing boy.
ex.zh: 警察把树林搜了个遍，寻找失踪的男孩。

ex.en: I [[scoured]] the shops for a present.
ex.zh: 我跑遍了商店找礼物。

vocab.def: to search a place or thing very carefully

cf.diff: search 是普通的“找”；scour 更强调把每个角落都翻遍，彻底、费力。

ex.en: I [[searched]] my bag for the keys.
ex.zh: 我在包里找钥匙。

vocab.zh: （市场的）空白、小众领域；合适的位置
vocab.note: 英式读 /niːʃ/，美式也读 /nɪtʃ/。a niche market（小众市场）、find your niche（找到适合自己的位置）。

ex.en: The shop serves a [[niche]] market of vinyl collectors.
ex.zh: 这家店服务黑胶唱片收藏者这个小众市场。

ex.en: She finally found her [[niche]] as a teacher.
ex.zh: 她终于找到了适合自己的位置：当老师。

vocab.def: a small area of business that few others are serving; a place or job that suits you

vocab.note: 专门繁殖、培育动物或植物的人：a dog breeder。动词 breed（繁殖、饲养）。

ex.en: We bought our puppy from a local [[breeder]].
ex.zh: 我们从本地一位饲养者那里买了小狗。

ex.en: Horse [[breeders]] travel to the show every year.
ex.zh: 养马人每年都来参加这个展会。

vocab.def: a person who keeps animals or plants in order to produce young ones

vocab.expr: 地点状语 + 动词 + 主语（倒装）
vocab.zh: 地点或方向状语提前，主谓倒装
vocab.note: 表示地点、方向的短语放在句首时，可以把动词放在主语前面，让描述更生动：Into the room walked a tall man.（走进屋来的是一个高个子男人。）常用动词：come, go, stand, sit, walk, lie 等，主语通常是名词而不是代词。

ex.en: [[Into]] the room walked a tall stranger.
ex.zh: 走进房间的是一个高个子陌生人。

ex.en: [[Into]] the garden ran three excited children.
ex.zh: 跑进花园的是三个兴奋的孩子。

vocab.conn: 地点 / 方向状语 + 不及物动词 + 名词主语（主语是代词时不倒装）
vocab.say: Into this niche stepped a breeder

pick.why: 地点状语 Under the tree 放句首，直接把动词 sat 提到主语前。
主语是代词时不倒装（应说 Out it jumped），所以选名词主语 a cat。

vocab.note: 失去家人或亲近的人：bereaved families（失去亲人的家庭）。the bereaved 指“死者家属”。

ex.en: The charity supports [[bereaved]] children.
ex.zh: 这家慈善机构帮助失去亲人的孩子。

ex.en: Our thoughts are with the [[bereaved]].
ex.zh: 我们的心与死者家属同在。

vocab.def: having recently lost a close relative or friend through death

vocab.note: be paired with：和……配成一对、搭配。也可以说菜和酒的搭配：fish paired with white wine。

ex.en: Each new student is [[paired with]] an older one.
ex.zh: 每个新生都会和一个高年级学生结对。

ex.en: This cheese [[pairs with]] red wine.
ex.zh: 这种奶酪配红酒。

vocab.def: to put two people or things together as a pair

vocab.note: 住在房东家里、付房租的人（常和房东同住）。动词 lodge（寄宿）。

ex.en: They took in a [[lodger]] to help pay the rent.
ex.zh: 他们招了个房客来分担房租。

ex.en: The [[lodger]] keeps to himself.
ex.zh: 那个房客不太和人来往。

vocab.def: a person who pays to live in a room in someone else's house

cf.diff: tenant 是租整套房子或店面的租户；lodger 通常是住在房东家里、租一个房间的人。

ex.en: The [[tenants]] complained about the heating.
ex.zh: 租户们抱怨暖气的问题。

vocab.note: put sth up for sale / for hire / for adoption：拿出来卖 / 出租 / 供人领养。

ex.en: Their house was [[put up for sale]] last week.
ex.zh: 他们的房子上周挂出来卖了。

ex.en: The puppies were [[put up for]] adoption.
ex.zh: 这些小狗被送出来供人领养。

vocab.def: to offer something to be sold, rented or adopted

vocab.note: faint 是“微弱的”：faintly amused（有点被逗乐）、faintly ridiculous（有点可笑）。

ex.en: The room smelled [[faintly]] of smoke.
ex.zh: 房间里有一点烟味。

ex.en: He looked [[faintly]] embarrassed.
ex.zh: 他看上去有点尴尬。

vocab.def: slightly; not very strongly

vocab.note: 作动词：address a problem / an issue（着手解决问题）。名词“地址”大家都熟，这个动词义更正式。

ex.en: The government must [[address]] the housing shortage.
ex.zh: 政府必须解决住房短缺问题。

ex.en: We need to [[address]] these complaints quickly.
ex.zh: 我们需要尽快处理这些投诉。

vocab.def: to think about a problem and start trying to deal with it

vocab.note: 从某事中得到好处的人：the main beneficiaries of the new law（新法的主要受益者）。也指遗嘱的受益人。

ex.en: Small shops were the biggest [[beneficiaries]] of the tax cut.
ex.zh: 减税最大的受益者是小商店。

ex.en: She named her niece as the [[beneficiary]] of her will.
ex.zh: 她在遗嘱里指定侄女为受益人。

vocab.def: a person who gets an advantage from something

cf.diff: 形近词：benefactor 是给钱、给帮助的人；beneficiary 是得到好处的人，正好相反。

ex.en: A wealthy [[benefactor]] paid for the new library.
ex.zh: 一位富有的捐助人出钱建了新图书馆。

vocab.note: 对别人（或动物）的关心和照顾，带点郑重的味道，很书面。

ex.en: She thanked the nurses for their [[solicitude]].
ex.zh: 她感谢护士们的悉心照顾。

ex.en: His [[solicitude]] for his elderly mother was touching.
ex.zh: 他对年迈母亲的关怀令人感动。

vocab.def: anxious care and concern for someone

vocab.note: 名词：a flock of sheep / birds。动词：People flocked to the beach.（人们成群涌向海滩。）

ex.en: A [[flock]] of geese flew over the lake.
ex.zh: 一群大雁飞过湖面。

ex.en: Tourists [[flock]] to the city every summer.
ex.zh: 每年夏天游客都蜂拥而至。

vocab.def: a group of birds or sheep; to go somewhere in large numbers

vocab.note: plunge sth into sth：把……猛地扔进去。也指价格“暴跌”：Prices plunged.

ex.en: She [[plunged]] her hands into the cold water.
ex.zh: 她把双手猛地浸进冷水里。

ex.en: Share prices [[plunged]] overnight.
ex.zh: 股价一夜之间暴跌。

vocab.def: to push or throw something suddenly into something; to fall suddenly

vocab.note: 本义是“打晕”；常用来表示“让人震惊”：We were stunned by the news.。形容词 stunning 是“极美的”。

ex.en: The bird was [[stunned]] when it flew into the window.
ex.zh: 那只鸟撞上窗户，被撞晕了。

ex.en: Everyone was [[stunned]] by the result.
ex.zh: 大家都被这个结果惊呆了。

vocab.def: to make a person or animal unconscious; to shock or surprise someone very much

cf.diff: stunned 是“被打晕的；惊呆的”；stunning 是“美得惊人的”：a stunning view。

ex.en: The view from the top is [[stunning]].
ex.zh: 山顶的风景美极了。

vocab.note: 英式说法 sit an exam / a test / a course：参加考试或课程。美式多说 take an exam。

ex.en: She will [[sit]] her final exams in June.
ex.zh: 她六月要参加期末考试。

ex.en: He [[sat]] the driving test three times.
ex.zh: 他考了三次驾照。

vocab.def: (British) to take an exam or a course

vocab.note: deride sb/sth as ...：嘲笑……是……。名词 derision（嘲笑）。比 laugh at 正式得多。

ex.en: His ideas were [[derided]] as unrealistic.
ex.zh: 他的想法被嘲笑为不切实际。

ex.en: Critics [[deride]] the film as boring.
ex.zh: 评论家嘲笑这部电影很无聊。

vocab.def: to say that someone or something is stupid or has no value

cf.diff: mock 常指当面取笑、模仿别人；deride 更正式，多用于公开批评、贬低某个观点或做法。

ex.en: The other kids [[mocked]] his accent.
ex.zh: 其他孩子取笑他的口音。

vocab.note: amok 读 /əˈmɒk/。原指人发狂乱砍乱杀；现在多比喻事情失控：bureaucracy run amok（官僚作风泛滥）。

ex.en: The goats [[ran amok]] in the garden.
ex.zh: 山羊在花园里横冲直撞。

ex.en: Without rules, things could [[run amok]].
ex.zh: 没有规则的话，事情可能会失控。

vocab.def: to behave in a wild and uncontrolled way

vocab.note: 政府机关里按规章办事的官员，常带贬义（死板、繁琐）。bureaucracy：官僚体制、繁文缛节。

ex.en: [[Bureaucrats]] in the capital make all the decisions.
ex.zh: 所有决定都由首都的官员做出。

ex.en: He's a [[bureaucrat]] who loves forms.
ex.zh: 他是个热爱填表格的官僚。

vocab.def: an official in a government department, often one who follows rules too strictly

cf.diff: bureaucrat 是人（官员）；bureaucracy 是制度或繁琐的手续。

ex.en: There's too much [[bureaucracy]] in this office.
ex.zh: 这个办公室的手续太繁琐了。

vocab.note: dictate what / how ...：硬性规定……。本义是“口述（让人记下）”。名词 dictator（独裁者）。

ex.en: You can't [[dictate]] what I wear.
ex.zh: 你不能规定我穿什么。

ex.en: The weather will [[dictate]] our plans.
ex.zh: 天气将决定我们的计划。

vocab.def: to tell someone what to do, often in an annoying way

vocab.note: 老鼠、松鼠、仓鼠、豚鼠都属于 rodents，特点是门牙一直长。

ex.en: Squirrels and mice are [[rodents]].
ex.zh: 松鼠和老鼠都是啮齿动物。

ex.en: The barn was full of [[rodents]].
ex.zh: 谷仓里到处是老鼠。

vocab.def: a small animal with sharp front teeth, such as a mouse or rat

vocab.note: 作动词：counter that ...（反驳说……）。名词“柜台”大家都熟。

ex.en: “That's not fair,” she [[countered]].
ex.zh: “这不公平。”她反驳道。

ex.en: He [[countered]] that the plan would save money.
ex.zh: 他反驳说这个计划能省钱。

vocab.def: to reply to criticism by giving a different opinion

vocab.note: lodge 作动词是“正式提交”：lodge a complaint / an appeal（提出投诉 / 上诉）。比 make a complaint 更正式。

ex.en: She [[lodged a complaint]] with the hotel manager.
ex.zh: 她向酒店经理正式投诉了。

ex.en: Several neighbours have [[lodged a complaint]] about the noise.
ex.zh: 好几位邻居就噪音提出了投诉。

vocab.def: to make an official complaint

vocab.note: un- + troubled（烦恼的）：不担心、不在乎：untroubled by criticism（不受批评困扰）。

ex.en: She seemed [[untroubled]] by the bad news.
ex.zh: 她似乎没被坏消息困扰。

ex.en: He slept an [[untroubled]] sleep.
ex.zh: 他睡得很安稳。

vocab.def: not worried or upset by something

vocab.note: 作动词：prize sth（非常看重）：prize honesty（看重诚实）。形容词 prized（珍贵的）。名词“奖品”大家都熟。

ex.en: Swiss watches are [[prized]] for their accuracy.
ex.zh: 瑞士手表因为精准而备受珍视。

ex.en: She [[prizes]] her independence.
ex.zh: 她非常看重自己的独立。

vocab.def: to think that something is very valuable or important

vocab.note: it is fitting that ...：……是很恰当的。比 suitable 更书面，常用于纪念、结尾。

ex.en: It was a [[fitting]] end to a wonderful day.
ex.zh: 这是美好一天的完美结尾。

ex.en: It seems [[fitting]] that she won on her birthday.
ex.zh: 她在生日那天获胜，真是恰如其分。

vocab.def: suitable or right for a particular situation

cloze.hint: 发现商机（___ a gap in the market）
倒装句开头的介词（___ this niche stepped）
拿出来出租（___ up for hire）

breakdown.en: Owners can end up trapped in an endless chain of guinea pigs, each new purchase prolonging the obligation by several years.
points: 主干：Owners can end up trapped in an endless chain —— 主人们最后可能被困在一条没完没了的链条里。
end up + 过去分词 / doing：最后落得……（end up 已学）。
each new purchase prolonging ...：独立主格结构（名词 + doing），有自己的“主语” each new purchase，补充说明结果。
prolong sth by + 时间：把……延长多久；by 表示差额。
